paths.description: Subcommand paths of one or two words, e.g. `ps` or `image ls`.

herdrWords.description: herdr options or subcommand paths of up to three words, e.g. `worktree create` or `plugin log list`.

hardWrite.description: Commands that modify files or system state whatever their arguments: blocked in read-only agents.

writeSubcommands.description: First non-option argument that makes a package manager modify dependencies or files.

write.description: git subcommands that modify the repository or working tree.

read.description: git subcommands for which a learned wildcard rule may be offered.

help.description: Options and command groups that only print help or the version when run exactly like this (or with --help): a rule may allow them as exact commands, never with a wildcard. Bare `herdr`, `herdr server`, `herdr update` are not help: they start something.

read.description: Read-only herdr subcommands: a rule may allow them with any arguments, and a wildcard may follow them.

ui.description: Subcommands that only change what herdr displays (a tab label, a notification). Allowed by the herdr-ui preset when opencode runs in a herdr pane, and accepted when the user lists them (inside herdr); never part of the shared allowlist.

write.description: herdr subcommands that write files, worktrees or the herdr installation: blocked in read-only agents.

environment.description: Variables handed to later commands. opencode never prompts for `export`, `declare` or a bare `NAME=value`, so the write guard blocks those that export a variable outside exportSafe, or give a new value to a variable that is exported.

exportSafe.description: Variables that only select a language, a format or turn a behaviour off, whatever their value: they may be exported or assigned. A trailing `*` matches a prefix (`LC_*`).

alwaysExported.description: Variables treated as exported even when the plugin's own environment lacks them: a new value always reaches later commands (zsh's `path` array is tied to PATH).

containers.description: Container engines with the same command line (docker, podman), judged by subcommand path.

read.description: Read-only subcommand paths: allow.json has `<name> <path> *` for each name. Global options must come before them, so a rule starting with the subcommand never covers -H/--host/--context.

write.description: Subcommand paths that change containers, images, volumes, networks, contexts or files: blocked in read-only agents (save and export only with -o/--output).

subcommandHelp.description: Subcommands whose exact `<program> <subcommand> --help` is allowed after the ask flags, because it only prints help. git also gets every subcommand in git.write and git.read, herdr every path in herdr.read and herdr.write and every `herdr <path> *` rule in ask.json (never the UI subcommands). A form already allowed by the rules before it is skipped.

mise.description: Subcommand paths of one or two words, e.g. `use` or `settings set`.

wildcardSafe.description: Commands for which /guard-review may offer a wildcard rule: all their read-only uses are safe, and their write flags are caught by ask.json or the guard.

rtkReadSubcommands.description: rtk subcommands that wrap a read-only command.
